Contemporaneous Record: Record created at or near the time of the event or work it describes.
Context Precision: Proportion of retrieved passages that are actually relevant to the question.
Context Recall: Proportion of the information needed to answer that was successfully retrieved.
Context Window: Maximum amount of tokenized input and output a model can handle in one request.
Contiguous Pile Wall: Retaining wall of closely spaced bored piles with small gaps between them.
Contingency Drawdown: Planned profile for the release of contingency over the project life cycle.
Contingency Reserve: Time or cost allowance within the baseline for identified uncertainty.
Continuing Effect: Characteristic of an event whose consequences persist, triggering obligations to submit interim particulars at intervals. [FIDIC]
Continuous Flow: Uninterrupted progression of a crew through locations without stopping or backtracking.
Contra Proferentem: Rule that ambiguity in a contract term is construed against the party who put it forward or who seeks to rely on it.
Contract Administrator: Person administering the construction contract, certifications, instructions, and time or payment procedures.
Contract Completion Date: Date by which the contractor is contractually required to complete, including valid extensions.
Contract Data: Contract-specific data completing variables, options, dates, and particulars in a standard form.
Contract Programme: Programme required by and administered under the construction contract.
Contract Sum Analysis: Breakdown of a design and build contract sum used for valuation and change assessment.
Contractor: Party responsible for carrying out the works under the contract.
Contractor Delay: Delay caused by an event allocated to the contractor under the contract.
Contractor Risk Event: An event whose time or cost consequences are allocated to the contractor under the contract.
Contractor's Proposals: Contractor's proposed design, method, and solution responding to the employer's requirements.
Contractor's Representative: Individual appointed by the contractor with authority to act on its behalf on site. [FIDIC]
Contractors All Risks: Insurance covering physical loss or damage to the works during construction.
Contractual Milestone: Milestone whose date is fixed by the contract and may carry damages or payment consequences.
Contraflow: Traffic arrangement running opposing flows on one carriageway during works.
Control Account: Management control point where scope, budget, actual cost, and schedule performance are integrated.
Control Account Manager: Person accountable for performance of a control account.
Control Account Plan: Detailed plan of work packages and planning packages within a control account.
Controlled Vocabulary: Approved set of terms used consistently for indexing and retrieval.
Coordinated Services Drawing: Drawing resolving the three-dimensional routing of all services within available zones.
Coordination Drawing: Drawing combining disciplines or systems to resolve spatial and interface coordination.
Core Bundle: Reduced bundle of the principal documents to which the tribunal will be taken.
Core Participant: Person or organisation designated by the inquiry chair as having a significant role or interest, with enhanced procedural rights.
Core Principles (SCL): Summary guidance principles at the front of the SCL Delay and Disruption Protocol covering programme and records, extension of time, concurrency, float, acceleration, disruption and global claims.
Coreference Resolution: Linking of pronouns and alternative descriptions to the entity they denote.
Corrective Action: Action taken to eliminate the cause of a detected nonconformance.
Correlation: Statistical dependency between modelled variables, which materially affects simulation output spread.
Correspondence: Letters, emails, notices, memoranda, and other communications exchanged or recorded on a project.
Correspondence Register: Index of incoming and outgoing letters, notices and emails with reference, date, subject and response tracking.
Corroboration: Independent evidence supporting a fact asserted by another source.
COSHH: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health.
Cosine Similarity: Measure of similarity between two vectors based on the angle between them, widely used to rank embeddings.
Cost Baseline: Approved time-phased project budget used to measure cost performance.
Cost Engineer: Practitioner responsible for cost estimating, budgeting, forecasting, and cost-control analysis.
Cost Loading: Assignment of budgeted cost to programme activities to derive a time-phased cost curve.
Cost Performance Index: Cost efficiency ratio calculated as earned value divided by actual cost.
Cost Performance Report: Formal periodic report of earned value data by control account.
Cost Plus Fee: Payment of actual cost plus an agreed fee, used where scope cannot be defined in advance.
Cost Plus Profit: Defined recovery basis comprising cost properly incurred plus a stated percentage for profit. [FIDIC]
Cost Records: Accounting and site records evidencing the resources and costs actually expended.
Cost Reimbursable Contract: Contract under which allowable actual costs are reimbursed with the agreed fee mechanism.
Cost Value Reconciliation: Periodic comparison of value earned against cost incurred to establish the true margin position.
Costain v Haswell: Costain Ltd v Charles Haswell & Partners Ltd [2009] EWHC 3140 (TCC); a claimant must prove delay to completion, not merely delay to an activity. [Case law]
Counsel to the Inquiry: Barrister or advocate appointed to assist the chair, lead the evidence and question witnesses.
Counter-Analysis: Opposing expert's analysis prepared in response to a delay or quantum analysis.
Counterclaim: Claim advanced in response to another party's claim.
Country of Origin: Source of manufacture, relevant to lead time, approval, tariffs and specification compliance.
Coupler: Mechanical device joining reinforcing bars end to end.
Court of Cassation: Highest court of appeal in UAE onshore jurisdictions, determining points of law.
Court-Appointed Expert: Expert appointed by a civil law court to investigate technical issues and report, often decisive in UAE construction litigation.
Cover: Distance between reinforcement and the concrete surface, governing durability and fire resistance.

Crane Oversail: Slewing of a crane jib over land outside the site boundary, requiring third party agreement.
Crashing: Schedule compression by adding resources for the least practical incremental cost.
Crawler Crane: Tracked crane suited to heavy lifts and repeated repositioning on prepared ground.
Crew Size Inefficiency: Productivity loss from operating crews at other than their optimum composition.
Critical Delay: Delay affecting a critical or driving path so that project or milestone completion moves unless recovered.
Critical Lift: Lift requiring enhanced planning because of weight, proximity, complexity or consequence of failure.
Critical Path: Longest or driving logic-linked sequence determining the relevant project or milestone completion date.

Cross Passage: Connection between parallel tunnel bores, generally provided for evacuation.
Cross-Examination: Questioning of a witness by the opposing party.
Crown: Highest internal surface of a tunnel arch.
Cruciality Index: Combined measure of an activity's criticality and its correlation with project completion.
Cube Test: Compressive strength test on a cast concrete specimen at a defined age.
Culpable Delay: Delay for which the contractor is responsible and which is not excusable under the contract.
Culvert: Structure conveying watercourse or drainage beneath an embankment or road.
Cumulative Delay: Total delay accrued to a milestone from all causes across the analysis period.
Cumulative Impact: Combined effect of multiple changes or events that is greater or harder to isolate than each event viewed separately.
Curing: Maintenance of moisture and temperature conditions allowing concrete to develop strength and durability.
Current Programme: Programme representing the latest available status and forecast.
Curtain Wall: Non-loadbearing external wall system carrying only its own weight and wind load to the structure.
Custodian: Individual or system from whose records a document set was collected.
Cut and Cover: Method excavating from the surface, constructing the structure, then reinstating the ground above.
Cut and Fill: Balancing of excavated material against material required for filling to minimise import and disposal.
CV: Cost Variance; earned value minus actual cost. [generic] | Cost Variance [generic]
Daily Huddle: Short daily coordination meeting between trade supervisors at the work face.
Daily Progress Report: Daily record of work, labour, plant, weather, deliveries, constraints, incidents, and progress.
Dangling Logic: Incomplete or discontinuous logic that leaves activity dates insufficiently driven through the network.
DART: Days Away, Restricted or Transferred rate.
Dashboard: Consolidated visual display of selected project performance metrics and exceptions.
Data Date: Boundary between actual progress and forecast work in a statused programme.
Data Drop: Scheduled issue of a defined information set at a project stage.
Data Residency: Requirement concerning the geographic location where data is stored or processed.

Data Window: Period of records or schedule status bounded by selected dates for analysis.
Daywork: Valuation of work based on recorded labour, plant, and materials at agreed rates and mark-ups.

DC: Document Control [generic] | Direct Current [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]

DDR: Design Deviation Request [generic] | Discipline Design Review [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]

Decision Log: Record of significant decisions, basis, authority, date, and affected scope.
Deduplication: Identification and removal or linking of duplicate records or files.

Delivery Note: Record accompanying or confirming delivery of materials or equipment.
Demolition: Controlled dismantling or removal of existing structures.
Dense Retrieval: Retrieval using learned vector embeddings to capture semantic similarity.
Dependency: Logical or practical relationship in which one item relies on another.
Depot: Facility for stabling, servicing, maintaining, and controlling vehicles or equipment.

Design Assurance: Planned independent or controlled activities providing confidence that design requirements and risks are properly addressed.

Design Responsibility Matrix: Matrix allocating design, review, approval, interface, and assurance responsibilities.

Detailed Design: Design developed to the detail needed for construction, fabrication, installation, or final approval.
Deterministic Engine: Calculation component expected to return the same output for the same validated input and configuration.
Deterministic Layer: Component producing computed, reproducible outputs from structured data, positioned upstream of any generated narrative. [toolkit]
Developer: Party promoting, funding and realising a development scheme.

Dewatering: Removal or control of groundwater or surface water to enable safe construction.
Dewatering Consent: Regulatory permission to abstract and discharge groundwater during construction.
DfMA: Design for Manufacture and Assembly; design approach optimising off-site production and rapid site assembly.
Diaphragm Wall: Reinforced concrete wall cast in a bentonite-supported trench, used for deep basements and cut-and-cover.
DIFC Courts: Common law courts of the Dubai International Financial Centre.
Differential Settlement: Unequal settlement between parts of a structure, capable of causing distortion and damage.
Digital Rehearsal: Simulation of a construction sequence in a model before execution to test constraints and safety.
Digital Twin: Digital representation of an asset connected to selected operational or lifecycle data.
Dilution of Supervision: Loss of productivity where supervisory capacity is spread across more work fronts or changed work than planned.
Direct Payment: Payment made by the employer to a subcontractor rather than through the main contractor.
Directed Acceleration: Acceleration expressly instructed by the employer or contract administrator.
Disallowed Cost: Cost excluded from Defined Cost because it was not properly incurred or falls within listed exclusions. [NEC]
Discharge: Written confirmation that the final statement represents full and final settlement, usually given with the final statement. [FIDIC]

Disclosure List: Schedule of documents disclosed, withheld or no longer in a party's control.
Discrete Disruption Analysis: Quantification of disruption on individual identified activities or areas rather than across the project as a whole.
Discrete Effort: Work with a specific end product against which objective progress can be measured.
Disposition: Decision on how a nonconformance is resolved, such as rework, repair, accept-as-is or reject.
Dispute Adjudication Board: FIDIC standing or ad hoc board deciding disputes under older contract editions.
Dispute Avoidance/Adjudication Board: FIDIC board supporting dispute avoidance and issuing decisions under 2017 forms.

Dispute Review Board: Board reviewing and recommending or deciding project disputes under the agreed rules.
Disruption: Loss of productivity or efficiency in carrying out work, which may occur with or without delay to completion.
District Cooling: Centralised chilled water production distributed to multiple buildings, common in Gulf developments.
Diversion Consent: Approval from a network operator for alteration of its apparatus.
Diversion from Landfill: Proportion of construction waste reused, recycled or recovered rather than landfilled.
Diversionary Works: Relocation of existing utility apparatus to accommodate new construction.
Dividing Date: NEC assessment boundary separating actual cost already incurred from forecast cost and programme effects.

Document Number: Controlled identifier assigned to a project document.
Document Population: Defined universe of documents subject to search, review or production.
Document Production: Process of requesting, searching, reviewing, and producing documents relevant to a dispute.
Document Reference: Controlled identifier or citation used to locate a project record.
Document Register: Controlled index of documents with revision, status, date and distribution.
Document Status: Code or description indicating review, approval, suitability, or issue purpose.
Domestic Subcontractor: Subcontractor freely selected and engaged by the main contractor.

Drawdown: Progressive consumption of a contingency, funding allocation or risk allowance.
Drawing Register: Controlled list of drawings, revisions, status, discipline, and issue dates.

Drone Survey: Aerial capture of site imagery and topography for progress, survey and volume measurement.
Dry Riser: Firefighting main charged by the fire service at the point of use.
Drywall: Partition and lining construction using plasterboard on metal or timber framing.
DTZ: DTZ Pieda, a firm of property management consultants who provided advice to CEC on funding of the ETP
Dubai Municipality: Municipal authority responsible for building permits, inspections and completion certificates in Dubai. [UAE]
Ductwork: Distribution system conveying air between plant and terminals.
Duration Change Register: Record of activity duration changes between programme revisions.
Duration Percent Complete: Progress measure based on original and remaining duration under the scheduling system's formula.
Duration Type: Setting controlling how duration, units and resource assignments interact when one is changed.
Duration Uncertainty: Inherent variability in activity durations modelled independently of discrete risk events.
Dust Suppression: Measures limiting airborne dust from construction operations.
Duty Holder: Party carrying defined statutory responsibilities for safety at a stage of a project.
Duty of Care: Obligation to exercise reasonable skill and care, arising in tort or by contractual term.

Dynamic Testing: Testing of vehicles in motion over the infrastructure, progressively increasing speed and system integration.

Earthing and Bonding: Connections limiting touch voltages and providing a fault current path.

Easement: Property right allowing specified use of another party's land.

Email Thread: Related sequence of email messages, replies, and attachments.
Email Threading: Grouping of related messages so that only the most inclusive message in a chain requires review.
Embedded Rail: Rail set within a continuous supporting material flush with the road surface, typical of on-street tramway.
Embedding: Numeric vector representation used to compare semantic similarity between text or other data.
Embodied Carbon: Greenhouse gas emissions associated with materials, transport, construction and end of life, excluding operational energy.
Emden Formula: A formula using the contractor's actual head-office-overhead and profit percentage to estimate unabsorbed overhead during delay.
Emergency Lighting: Lighting operating on loss of normal supply to permit safe evacuation.
Emergency Response Plan: Arrangements for responding to fire, injury, rescue, spillage and evacuation.
Emiratisation: Policy requiring defined proportions of UAE nationals in the private sector workforce. [UAE]

Fabrication Drawing: Shop drawing giving the detailed geometry and connection details for manufacture.
Facade Access: Permanent or temporary means of reaching the external envelope for installation and maintenance.
Facade Performance Testing: Programme of air, water and structural testing on a representative facade sample.
Face Support Pressure: Pressure maintained at the tunnel face to prevent collapse and limit ground movement.
Factory Acceptance Test: Testing of equipment at the manufacturer's works before shipment.
Factual Witness: Witness giving evidence primarily of facts personally known or observed.
Fair Valuation: Valuation on a reasonable basis where contract rates are not applicable.
Faithfulness: Degree to which a generated statement is supported by the retrieved source material.
Fall Arrest: System limiting the consequences of a fall where prevention is not practicable.
Falsework: Temporary structure supporting formwork and the loads imposed during construction.
Fast Tracking: Schedule compression by overlapping work that was originally planned sequentially.
FASTA: Fire Alarm System Testing and Approval
FCU: Fan Coil Unit; local terminal unit conditioning air within a zone.
Federal Arbitration Law: Federal Law No. 6 of 2018 on Arbitration, the principal arbitration statute for onshore UAE. [UAE]
Federated Model: Combined model referencing discipline or package models without necessarily merging authorship.
Fee Percentage: Percentage applied to Defined Cost to cover overheads and profit. [NEC]
Feeding Buffer: Buffer placed where a non-critical chain joins the critical chain.
Few-Shot Prompting: Prompting technique supplying worked examples to demonstrate the required output form.
FIDIC: Federation Internationale Des Ingenieurs-Conseils [generic] | International Federation of Consulting Engineers. [generic]

FIDIC Red Book: FIDIC form traditionally used for employer-designed construction works.

Field Density Test: In-situ test confirming that placed fill has achieved the specified compaction.
File Hash: Cryptographic digest used to identify a file and detect change.
Final Acceptance: Acceptance following expiry of the defects period and closure of all outstanding obligations.
Final Account: Agreed or determined final valuation of the contract, including changes, claims, and adjustments.
Final Business Case: UK business-case stage confirming the final deal, costs, benefits, risk, and implementation arrangements.
Final Date for Payment: Date by which a notified sum must be paid.
Final Payment Certificate: Certificate stating the final amount due under the contract.
Final Statement: Contractor's final account submission setting out all sums considered due. [FIDIC]
Financial Case: Business case component confirming affordability and funding.
Financing Charges: Cost of funding a shortfall in cash flow caused by delayed or withheld payment.
Fine Tuning: Post-handover adjustment of systems to achieve stable and efficient operation.
Fine-Tuning: Further training of a model on task-specific data to adjust its behaviour.
Finish Float: Difference between late finish and early finish.
Finish Milestone: Zero-duration activity representing completion of a project phase, obligation, or event.
Finish On: Constraint placing an activity finish on a specified date under P6 rules.
Finish On or After: Constraint preventing an activity from finishing before a specified date.
Finish On or Before: Constraint preventing an activity from finishing after a specified date.
Finish-to-Finish: Relationship in which the successor cannot finish until the predecessor finishes, subject to lag.
Finish-to-Start: Relationship in which the successor cannot start until the predecessor finishes, subject to lag.
Fire Alarm System: Detection, control and alarm installation warning occupants of fire.
Fire Engineering: Performance-based analysis demonstrating fire safety where prescriptive guidance is not followed.
Fire Protection to Steel: Applied or encasing protection maintaining the load capacity of steelwork for a specified fire period.
Fire Strategy: Document setting out how a building achieves fire safety through means of escape, compartmentation, suppression and access.
Firestopping: Sealing of penetrations and joints to maintain the fire resistance of a separating element.
First Fix: Services and joinery installed before wall and ceiling finishes are closed.
First-in-Time Approach: Approach treating the delay event that first became an effective cause of critical delay as determinative.
Fit-Out: Works converting a completed structural shell into occupiable space.
Five Case Model: Business case structure comprising strategic, economic, commercial, financial and management cases. [UK]
Fixed Formula: Earned value technique claiming a set proportion at start and the remainder at completion, such as 0/100 or 50/50.
Flashing: Sheet material weathering a junction or penetration in the envelope.
Float Consumption: Use or loss of available float as activities or events move later.
Float Erosion: Reduction in float between programme revisions or analysis periods.
Float Ownership: Contractual question of which party may use available programme float.
Float Path: P6 identifier for a ranked path affecting the selected completion point.
Float Path Order: P6 sequence number showing an activity's order within a calculated float path.
Float Suppression: Practice of concealing available float through constraints, artificial logic or extended durations.
Flow-Down: Transmission of main contract obligations into subcontracts.
Flowline: Line on a time-location chart representing the progress of a crew or trade through locations.
Fluctuations: Contractual mechanism adjusting the price for changes in the cost of labour, materials or taxes.
Flushing: Cleaning of pipework systems to remove debris before commissioning.

Force Majeure: An exceptional event beyond a party's control whose consequences depend on the governing contract and law.
Forecast: Current prediction of a future date, cost, quantity, or outcome.
Forecast Drift: Progressive movement of a forecast date across programme revisions.
Foreign Key: Field linking a record to a key in another table.
Forensic Planner: Planner specializing in retrospective or dispute-related schedule investigation.
Forensic Schedule Analysis: Investigation of how events interacted with a CPM model and actual project execution to explain schedule deviation.
Forensic Schedule Analysis Method: Named technique for retrospectively establishing the cause, extent and criticality of delay from programme and progress records.
Foreseeability: Test concerning whether an event or type of loss was reasonably foreseeable at the relevant time.
Formal Reprogramming: Controlled process of resetting the performance measurement baseline.
Formation Level: Prepared surface at the base of an excavation on which subsequent construction is founded.
Formula Approach: Calculation of unabsorbed head office overhead using a published formula rather than actual records.
Formwork: Temporary mould into which concrete is placed and which shapes it until it can support itself.
Forward Pass: CPM calculation of earliest activity dates from the project start through successor logic.
FP: Forth Ports, alternative name for FPA
Fragnet: Small logic-linked network representing a delay event or added scope for insertion into a programme.
Framework Agreement: Umbrella arrangement setting terms under which individual works packages may be called off.
Free Float: Time an activity can be delayed without delaying the early date of an immediate successor.
Free Issue Materials: Materials supplied by one party for installation by another, with associated risk and delay interfaces.
Fully Detailed Claim: Complete submission of contractual basis, factual narrative and supporting particulars required to substantiate a claim. [FIDIC]
Function Calling: Model capability to emit a structured call to a defined external tool and consume its result.
Functional Concurrency: Overlapping delay effects that are treated as concurrent for analysis even if their initiating events do not start simultaneously.
Fuzzy Matching: Approximate string comparison tolerating spelling and formatting variation.
Gabion: Wire basket filled with stone used for retaining, erosion control or scour protection.
Galvanising: Application of a zinc coating for corrosion protection.
Gantt Chart: Bar chart presenting activities against a time axis, optionally showing logic, float and progress.
Gate Booking: Reservation of a delivery slot, whose availability can constrain installation sequences.
Gateway 2: Pre-construction approval stage for higher-risk buildings, at which the regulator must approve before works may start. [UK]
Gateway 3: Completion approval stage for higher-risk buildings, required before occupation. [UK]
Gateway Review: Independent assurance review at a defined project lifecycle point.
General Conditions: Standard general contractual terms governing the agreement.
General Damages: Unliquidated damages requiring proof of breach, causation, remoteness, and loss.
Genuine Pre-Estimate of Loss: Traditional test for the enforceability of liquidated damages, now subsumed within the legitimate interest test.
Geogrid: Polymer grid used to reinforce soil and distribute load.
Geotechnical Baseline Report: Document defining the contractually assumed ground conditions against which actual conditions are compared for risk allocation.
Geotextile: Permeable fabric used for separation, filtration, drainage or reinforcement in ground works.
Glazing: Installation of glass units into a facade or opening.
Global Assessment: Broad evaluation of loss where individual causal links cannot be established, permitted only in restricted circumstances.
Global Calendar: Calendar available across multiple projects in a P6 database.
Global Change: Bulk automated modification of activity or resource data across a project.
Global Claim: A claim presenting aggregated loss from multiple events without fully linking each loss to each event.
Golden Dataset: Curated set of questions with verified answers used to measure system performance over time.
Golden Thread: Maintained, accurate and accessible building information required through design, construction and occupation. [UK]
Good Faith: Obligation, express or implied and prominent in civil law jurisdictions, to perform and enforce the contract honestly and fairly.
Goods Received Note: Record confirming receipt of materials on site against an order.
Governance: Framework of authority, accountability, decision-making, control, and oversight for a project or organization.
Governing Law: Law chosen by the parties to govern the substance of the contract.
Government of Dubai Conditions of Contra: Standard conditions used for Dubai government works, based on older FIDIC drafting with significant amendments. [UAE]
Green Amber Red Trigger: Tiered monitoring response regime defining review, action and stop levels.
Green Book: HM Treasury guidance on appraisal and evaluation of policies, programmes and projects. [UK]
Greenfield: Work on an undeveloped site without existing operational constraints.
Grid Connection: Physical and contractual connection of a generating asset to the transmission or distribution network.
GRIP: Governance for Railway Investment Projects; Network Rail's former eight-stage project lifecycle framework.
Grooved Rail: Rail section with a flangeway groove, used where track is embedded in a trafficked surface.
Gross Method: Delay measurement that reports total slippage in a period without deducting concurrent delay, mitigation or acceleration. [AACE 29R-03]
Ground Anchor: Tensioned element installed into competent ground to restrain a retaining structure.
Ground Bearing Pressure: Load imposed by plant on the ground, governing the need for mats or piled platforms.
Ground Improvement: Treatment of weak ground to increase strength, reduce settlement or mitigate liquefaction.
Ground Treatment: Pre-excavation improvement of ground ahead of or around a tunnel to permit safe advance.
Ground Truth: Verified correct answer against which system output is scored.
Grounding: Constraining output to identified source material, structured data, or deterministic results.
Groundwater Control: Measures to lower, exclude or manage groundwater to permit excavation in the dry.
Grout Duct: Sheathing containing post-tensioning tendons, grouted after stressing for protection.
Grouting: Injection of cementitious or chemical material to fill voids, strengthen ground or control water.
Guaranteed Maximum Price: Maximum price payable subject to stated exclusions, allowances, and approved changes.
Guardrail: Control constraining model inputs or outputs to enforce policy, scope or format.
Hadley v Baxendale: (1854) 9 Exch 341; two-limb test for remoteness of damage in contract. [Case law]
Half-Step Implementation: Time impact implementation that inserts a delay fragnet into a programme statused to the date immediately before the event.
Hallucination: Model output presented as factual despite lacking support or being incorrect.
Hammock Activity: Summary activity spanning from one event to another, often used for time-related support or reporting.
Handback: Return of infrastructure to operational control at the end of an access period, subject to defined conditions.
Handover: Controlled transfer of completed works, information, access, responsibility, and operational readiness.
Handover Certificate: Document recording transfer of an area, system or asset from one party to another.
Handover Certificate (Scaffold): Certificate confirming a scaffold has been erected in accordance with its design and inspected.
Handover Documentation: Complete record set issued at completion, including as-builts, manuals, certificates and warranties.
Handover Pack: Documentation issued to a purchaser or occupier at handover of a unit.
Hard Constraint: Constraint that can override network-driven dates, such as mandatory start or finish.
Hard Logic: Dependency dictated by physical or technical necessity.
Hazard Log: Living register of identified hazards, their controls, residual risk and closure evidence.
Head Office Overheads: Business-wide indirect costs not directly allocated to production on one project.
Health and Safety File: Record of information for those who will maintain, alter or demolish the structure in future.
Hearing Bundle: Compiled and paginated set of documents used at a hearing.
Hearsay: Evidence of a statement made out of the proceedings, adduced to prove the truth of its content.
Heat Stress: Physiological effect of high temperature and humidity on workforce output and safety.
Height Restriction: Limit on the height of plant and structures imposed by aviation or other safeguarding requirements.
HGCRA: Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996; the UK Construction Act.
High Density Planning: Detailed planning of imminent work at activity and resource level.
Higher-Risk Building: Building meeting statutory height and use criteria and subject to the enhanced safety regime. [UK]
Hijri Calendar: Lunar Islamic calendar governing the timing of religious holidays, which shift approximately eleven days earlier each Gregorian year. [UAE]
Hindsight: Knowledge of subsequent events used in retrospective analysis; a point of contention where the contract requires prospective assessment.
Hit Miss Ratio: Proportion of activities that completed on or before their baseline finish date.
Hoarding: Temporary boundary enclosure securing and screening a site.
Hoist: Vertical transport for materials or personnel on a building under construction.
Hold Point: Point beyond which work may not proceed without the release of the nominated party.
Honeycombing: Voided concrete surface caused by inadequate compaction or grout loss, requiring assessment and repair.
Horizontal Directional Drilling: Steerable trenchless technique installing ducts or pipes along a curved bore.
Hot Tubbing: Concurrent expert evidence in which opposing experts are questioned together by the tribunal.
Hot Works Permit: Permit controlling activities generating heat, flame or sparks.
HSE: Health Safety and Environment [generic] | Health, Safety and Environment. [generic] | Health and Safety Executive [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
HSEQ: Health, Occupational Safety, Environment and Quality
Hudson Formula: A formula using the tender head-office-overhead and profit percentage to estimate unabsorbed overhead during delay.
Human in the Loop: Workflow requiring human review, confirmation, correction, or approval of automated output.
HV Cable: High voltage cable connecting substations and primary distribution.
HVAC: Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning [generic] | Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning. [generic]
Hybrid Search: Search combining lexical or keyword retrieval with semantic vector retrieval.
HyDE: Hypothetical Document Embeddings; retrieval technique embedding a generated hypothetical answer to find similar real passages.
IBA Rules: IBA Rules on the Taking of Evidence in International Arbitration; widely adopted framework for documents, witnesses and experts.
ICC: International Chamber of Commerce; arbitration institution and rules. | Institution of Civil Engineers (see ICE).
ICE: Institute of Civil Engineers | Institution of Civil Engineers conditions of contract [contract form]

IChemE Forms: Institution of Chemical Engineers standard forms used for process plant projects.
Idle Plant: Plant retained on site but unable to be productively used.
IFC (BIM): Industry Foundation Classes open data schema for BIM information exchange.
Ikarian Reefer: National Justice Compania Naviera SA v Prudential Assurance Co Ltd (1993); statement of the duties and responsibilities of expert witnesses. [Case law]
Immutable Source: Preserved source file or record that the analytical workflow does not overwrite.
Impacted As-Planned: Additive method inserting delay events into the as-planned programme to model their calculated effect.
Impacted Programme: Programme after a modeled event or fragnet has been inserted or otherwise applied.
Implemented Compensation Event: Compensation event that has been assessed and incorporated into the Prices and any Completion Date, and which is not normally revisited. [NEC]
Import Clearance: Customs process governing release of imported materials, a recognised delay risk on international projects.
In-Situ Concrete: Concrete cast in its final position on site.
Incident Investigation: Structured enquiry into an incident to establish causes and prevent recurrence.
Incremental EOT Assessment: Periodic assessment and adjustment of time entitlement as the foreseeable effect of an event unfolds.
Incremental Launching: Bridge construction pushing a deck built behind an abutment out across the piers.
Indemnity: Undertaking to make good defined losses suffered by another party.
Independent Competent Person: Suitably qualified party engaged to provide independent assessment of safety-related design or works.
Independent Estimate at Completion: Statistically derived forecast of final cost used to test the project team's own estimate.
Independent Float: Time an activity can slip without affecting predecessors' late dates or successors' early dates.
Indexation: Adjustment of prices by reference to a published cost index.
Industry Studies Method: Disruption quantification using published research factors rather than project-specific measurement, generally ranked lowest in the hierarchy of methods.
Inefficiency: Use of more resources or time than reasonably required to achieve the same output.
Information Exchange: Defined delivery of information at an agreed stage against agreed requirements.
Information Manager: Role responsible for the information standards, processes and CDE on a project.
Information Release Schedule: Schedule stating when the employer will release design information to the contractor.
Informed Client: Client organisation with sufficient in-house capability to specify, challenge and control its delivery partners.

Inquiries Act 2005: UK statute governing the establishment, powers and conduct of statutory public inquiries.

Inquiry Rules 2006: Rules made under the Inquiries Act 2005 covering core participants, evidence, warning letters and inquiry records.
Insertion Method: Additive modelling in which delay fragnets are inserted into a programme to model their effect on completion.
Insolvency: Inability to pay debts as they fall due, triggering contractual termination and step-in provisions.
Inspection and Test Plan: Schedule of inspections, tests, acceptance criteria, responsibilities and records for an activity.
Installed Quantity: Measured quantity of work physically installed and accepted or recorded.
Instruction Register: Log of contractual or technical instructions, dates, authority, scope, status, and effects.
Instrumentation and Monitoring: Installation of sensors to measure ground and structural movement, water pressure and vibration during construction.
Insulated Glazing Unit: Sealed assembly of two or more glass panes separated by a spacer and cavity.
Integrated Baseline Review: Joint review confirming that the performance measurement baseline is realistic and that risks are understood.

Integrated Systems Testing: Testing of interconnected systems operating together under simulated conditions.
Interface Agreement: Agreement defining responsibilities, deliverables and timing where two contracts or parties meet.
Interface Detail: Junction between the work of two trades or packages, requiring coordinated design and sequence.

Interface Milestone: Milestone marking the point at which one party's work must be available to another.
Interface Register: Register of technical, organizational, contractual, and physical interfaces and their owners.
Interfering Float: Portion of total float that, if used, delays successor early dates but not project completion.
Interim Claim: Partial submission of a continuing claim pending final quantification. [FIDIC]

Interim Valuation: Periodic assessment of the value of work executed for payment purposes.
Interlocking: Signalling arrangement preventing conflicting movements from being authorised simultaneously.
Interpretation Layer: Regenerable layer converting evidence into probable sequence, driving relationships and criticality, distinct from the immutable evidence beneath it. [toolkit]
Intumescent Coating: Fire protection coating that expands when heated to insulate structural steel.

Investment Decision Point: Governance milestone at which funding is committed for the next stage of a project.
Invitation to Tender: Formal invitation for suppliers or contractors to submit a tender.
IR: Instruction Register [generic] | Inspection Request or Inspection Report, depending on project usage. [generic]
Ironmongery: Door and window hardware including hinges, closers, locks and access control furniture.
ISO 14001: International standard for environmental management systems.
ISO 19650: International standard for information management using building information modelling.
ISO 27001: International standard for information security management systems.
ISO 45001: International standard for occupational health and safety management systems.
ISO 9001: International standard for quality management systems.
Isolation: Removal of electrical supply from part of a system to allow safe working.
Issue Register: Log of current issues requiring decisions, actions, or escalation.
Jailbreak: Input crafted to induce a model to bypass its constraints.
JCT: Joint Contracts Tribunal; publisher of standard form building contracts widely used in the UK.
Jet Grouting: Ground improvement forming soil-cement columns by high-pressure injection.
Jetty: Structure projecting into water providing berthing or access.
John Doyle v Laing: John Doyle Construction Ltd v Laing Management (Scotland) Ltd [2004] ScotCS; treatment of global claims and partial failure of causation. [Case law]
Joinery: Manufactured timber elements such as doors, frames, panelling and fitted furniture.
Joint Statement: Document recording matters agreed and disagreed by experts after a joint meeting.
Joint Venture: Arrangement in which two or more parties combine resources and responsibility for a project or business purpose.
Jumpform: Formwork system climbing in discrete lifts, used for cores and shafts.
Jury Verdict: Award of a broad-brush sum where precise quantification is impossible, used sparingly and generally disfavoured.
Just in Time Delivery: Delivery of materials immediately before installation to minimise on-site storage.
Kerb: Edge element separating carriageway from footway or verge.
Key Date: Date by which a defined condition must be met; in NEC it is a contractual mechanism distinct from Completion.
Key Date (NEC): NEC contractual date by which stated conditions must be met, with defined cost consequences for failure.
Keyword Search: Retrieval based on exact terms, tokens, or lexical scoring.
Kinematic Envelope: Space swept by a vehicle allowing for suspension movement, wear and permitted tolerances.
Knowledge Graph: Structured representation of entities and their relationships, queryable independently of source text.
KPMG: A firm of financial and professional advisors who at times assisted the Scottish Executive with its reviews of the ETP
Labour Only Subcontract: Subcontract providing workforce only, with materials supplied by others.
Labour Return: Record of labour headcount, hours, trade, employer, and work location.

Land Acquisition: Process of obtaining the interests in land required for a scheme, by agreement or compulsion.
Landside: Area of an airport accessible without passing security control.

Lap Length: Overlap required between reinforcing bars to transfer force.
Laser Scanning: Survey technique capturing dense three-dimensional geometry of existing conditions.

Latent Defects Insurance: Insurance covering inherent defects discovered after completion.
Launch Chamber: Structure from which a tunnelling machine begins its drive.
Laydown Area: Designated area for receipt, storage and preassembly of materials.
Layout: Saved arrangement of columns, filters, grouping and bars in the scheduling tool.
Layout Parsing: Interpretation of document structure such as headings, columns, headers and footnotes prior to chunking.

Leading Indicator: Predictive safety measure such as observations, inspections and close calls.
Lean Construction: Production philosophy maximising value and minimising waste through reliable workflow.
Learning Curve: Improvement in unit productivity as a crew repeats an operation, and its loss when work is interrupted or resequenced.
LEED: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design
Legal Advice Privilege: Protection from disclosure of confidential communications between lawyer and client for the purpose of giving or obtaining legal advice.
Legal Hold: Instruction suspending routine disposal of potentially relevant records.
Legal Professional Privilege: Protection from disclosure for qualifying confidential lawyer-client communications or litigation materials.
Leonard Study: Research relating loss of labour productivity to the number and magnitude of change orders, used as an industry study benchmark.
Lessons Learned Register: Record of observations and recommendations captured for current and future projects.

Letter of Award: Communication confirming acceptance of a tender, sometimes preceding execution of the contract.
Letter of Intent: Pre-contract letter recording intention and possibly limited authority to proceed.

Levenshtein Distance: Count of single-character edits required to transform one string into another.

Lightning Protection: System conducting lightning discharge safely to earth.

Line List: Register of every pipeline in a plant with its service, size, material and design conditions.

Liquidated and Ascertained Damages: A pre-agreed contractual amount payable for delay under common UK drafting.

Liquidation: Insolvency procedure winding up a company and distributing its assets.
Literal Concurrency: Two delay events occurring at exactly the same time and both effective causes of delay to completion.
Litigation: Court process for resolving legal claims and disputes.
Litigation Privilege: Protection from disclosure of communications made for the dominant purpose of actual or contemplated litigation.
LLAU: Limits of Land to be Acquired or Used
LLM-as-Judge: Use of a model to score outputs against a rubric, calibrated against human review.
Load Bank Test: Testing of generators and power systems under artificial load.
Load File: Structured file accompanying a disclosure set, mapping document images to their metadata and text.
Load Schedule: Tabulation of connected and diversified electrical loads by circuit and board.
Location-Based Management System: Planning and control method organising work by location, using flowlines and continuous crew flow.

Logic Density: Ratio of relationships to activities, used as an indicator of network completeness.

LOI: Letter of Intent [generic] | Level of Information. [BIM]

Loop Check: Verification of a control loop from field device through to the control system.

Loss of Productivity: Reduction in output per unit of labour, equipment, or time compared with an appropriate benchmark.
Lost in the Middle: Observed degradation in a model's use of information positioned in the middle of a long context.
Lost Time Injury: Injury resulting in absence from work beyond the day of the incident.
Low Density Planning: Outline planning of work beyond the near-term horizon, pending further design and information.

Made Ground: Ground formed of previously deposited or engineered fill rather than natural strata.
Magnetic Particle Inspection: Non-destructive method detecting surface and near-surface flaws in ferrous material.

Main Option: One of the NEC pricing options A to F determining the payment mechanism. [NEC]

Supervisor (NEC): Defined NEC role checking compliance with the Scope and managing tests and defects.
Supplier: Party providing materials, equipment, products, or related services.
Supplier Document Register: Register of vendor or supplier documents, required dates, review status, and revisions.
Supplier Document Requirements List: Contract list defining supplier document deliverables, codes, dates, and review requirements.
Supply and Fix: Subcontract covering both provision and installation of materials.
Supply Chain Insolvency: Failure of a supplier or subcontractor, a recurring cause of delay and additional cost.
Supply Only: Subcontract covering provision of materials without installation.
Surface Course: Uppermost pavement layer providing skid resistance and ride quality.
Surveillance: Ongoing monitoring of a supplier or subcontractor's compliance with quality requirements.
Suspend Date: Actual date on which work on an in-progress activity stopped.
Suspended Ceiling: Ceiling hung below the structural soffit creating a service void.
Suspension: Temporary stopping of work or obligations under a contractual or legal right or instruction.
SV: Schedule Variance in earned-value terms; earned value minus planned value. [generic] | Schedule Variance [generic]

SW KIWR: Scottish Water Key Issues Weekly Review
Swept Path: Area occupied by a vehicle as it negotiates a curve, critical for on-street clearances and highway design.
Switchgear: Assembly of switching and protective devices controlling electrical circuits.
Synchro: 4D construction modelling software linking programme activities to model geometry.
System Assurance: Coordinated process demonstrating that reliability, availability, maintainability and safety requirements are satisfied.
System Boundary: Defined limit of a system for the purposes of completion, testing and handover.
System Dynamics Modelling: Simulation of feedback effects such as rework, overtime fatigue and schedule pressure on project productivity.
System Handover: Formal transfer of a completed and tested system to the operator, with documentation and training.
System Prompt: Highest-level application instruction defining model role, constraints, and behavior.
Systems Completion: Progressive completion and handover of the works by functional system rather than by area.
Systems Integration: Coordination and verification that interacting technical systems operate together as required.
T&C: Terms and Conditions [generic] | Testing and Commissioning [generic]
TAB: Testing, Adjusting and Balancing of building services systems.
Table Extraction: Recovery of structured rows and columns from documents where tables are represented visually.
Table Form: Large prefabricated soffit formwork panel moved between floors by crane.
Tabreed: National Central Cooling Company; district cooling provider in the UAE. [UAE]
Taking Off: Process of measuring quantities from drawings to compile a bill of quantities.
Taking Over: Employer or client acceptance of the works or section for use under the contract mechanism.
Taking-Over Certificate: FIDIC certificate recording taking over of the works or a section.
Takt Planning: Production planning method dividing work into equal-duration zones through which trades move at a fixed rhythm.
Takt Time: Fixed interval at which each trade moves from one zone to the next under takt planning.
Tanking: Continuous waterproof barrier applied to below-ground structure.
Target Cost: Cost target used in pain-share or gain-share and other incentivized contract mechanisms.
Target Programme: Internal or contractual programme establishing target dates that may be earlier than contractual dates.
TASK: P6 XER table containing activity records.
Task Dependent Activity: P6 activity whose dates are primarily driven by the activity calendar and logic.
Task Information Delivery Plan: Schedule of information deliverables for a single task team.
TASKACTV: P6 XER table linking activities to activity-code values.
TASKPRED: P6 XER table containing predecessor-successor relationship records.
TASKRSRC: P6 XER table containing activity-resource assignments.
Taxiway: Route connecting runways with aprons and other airport facilities.
TB&PDG: Tram Briefing and Project Delivery Group
TB&PDGJM: Tram Briefing and Project Delivery Group Joint Meeting
TC: Target Cost [generic] | Tram Communications [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
TCC: Technology and Construction Court; specialist English court for construction and engineering disputes.
TCPI: To-Complete Performance Index; cost efficiency required on remaining work to achieve a selected target. [generic] | To-Complete Performance Index [generic]
Technical Approval: Formal approval of technical design by the authorized body or reviewer.
Technical Query: Formal request to clarify a technical requirement, design, interface, or discrepancy.
Technical Submittal: Submission of product data, calculations or drawings for review before procurement or installation.
Technology Assisted Review: Use of machine learning to prioritise or classify documents for review.
Temperature: Sampling parameter controlling randomness in generation; low values favour determinism.
Temporary Bracing: Restraint installed during erection until the permanent stability system is complete.
Temporary Power: Construction-stage electrical supply, whose replacement by permanent power often governs commissioning.
Temporary Works: Works needed to enable construction but not normally forming part of the completed permanent asset.
Temporary Works Coordinator: Person coordinating control of temporary-works design, checking, implementation, and permits.
Temporary Works Design: Engineering design of the temporary structures needed to construct the permanent works.
Temporary Works Register: Register of all temporary works items with design status, check category and permit to load.
Temporary Works Supervisor: Person supervising temporary-works implementation under the project procedure.
Tender Addendum: Formal amendment or clarification issued to tender documents before bid submission.
Tender Analysis: Comparison and normalisation of tenders to a common basis before recommendation.
Tender Programme: Programme submitted with a bid showing the tenderer's proposed sequence and timing.
Terminal Float: Float between planned Completion and the Completion Date, owned by the contractor under NEC. [NEC]
Termination: Ending contractual performance under a contractual or legal right.
Terms of Reference: Document defining tribunal mandate, issues, parties, and procedure under some arbitration rules.
Test Certificate: Record evidencing that a test was performed and its result.
Testing and Commissioning: Integrated testing, verification, setting-to-work, and performance demonstration before handover.
Thermal Bridge: Path of increased heat transfer through the envelope, affecting energy performance and condensation risk.
Thickening: Additional management or supervisory resource applied to a project beyond that priced, claimed as a discrete cost.
Third Party Agreement: Agreement with a landowner, utility, operator or authority whose consent or cooperation is required for the works.
Third Party Rights: Statutory alternative to collateral warranties conferring benefits directly on named beneficiaries.
Three Lines of Defence: Governance model separating operational management, oversight functions and independent assurance.
Three-Point Estimate: Estimate expressed as optimistic, most likely and pessimistic values for use in probabilistic analysis.
Three-Week Look-Ahead: Short-term programme detailing work, constraints, and commitments for the next three weeks.
Tidal Window: Period within the tidal cycle during which a marine operation can be undertaken.

tie Change: Change instructed or deemed instructed by tie under the Infraco Contract change mechanism. [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]

Tie-In: Connection of new work into existing operating plant, usually requiring a shutdown window.
Tilos: Software for time-location and time-chainage planning of linear projects.
Time at Large: Situation in which the contractual completion date may cease to bind and completion is required within a reasonable time.
Time Bar: A contractual or statutory deadline whose effect may limit or extinguish a claim or remedy.
Time for Completion: Period within which the works or a section must be completed, measured from the commencement date and extended by any award of extension of time. [FIDIC]
Time Impact Analysis: Prospective or contemporaneous method inserting a fragnet into the current accepted update to calculate incremental completion impact.
Time Risk Allowance: Additional time included for contractor-owned risk within an activity or programme under the adopted planning approach.
Time Slice Analysis: Window-based examination of critical path and delay during successive periods using contemporaneous updates.
Time Slice Windows Analysis: SCL Protocol method dividing the project into consecutive windows and identifying the contemporaneous critical path and delay incurred in each. [SCL Protocol]
Time-Chainage Diagram: Planning chart plotting time against linear distance, used for roads, rail, tunnels and pipelines.
Time-Distant Analysis: Analysis carried out significantly after the event or its effects, often requiring retrospective methods and stronger record validation.
Time-Related Cost: Cost that varies with the duration of the works rather than with quantity.
Timesheet: Record of labour or equipment time by person, activity, cost code, or location.
TMT: Transport Management Team [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry] | Tram Management Team [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
To-Complete Performance Index: Cost efficiency required on remaining work to achieve a selected BAC or EAC target.
TOG: Tram Operations Group [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry] | Tram Oversight Group [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
Token: Unit of text processed by a language model or tokenizer.
Toolbox Talk: Short briefing to a work crew on a specific hazard, method or lesson learned.
Top-Down Construction: Method building permanent floor slabs progressively downward to prop the retaining walls as excavation proceeds.
Top-k: Number of highest-scoring candidates returned by a retrieval step.
Tornado Chart: Ranked bar chart showing the relative sensitivity of an outcome to uncertain inputs.
Total Cost Claim: A claim calculated as actual total cost minus tender or planned cost, subject to strict evidential qualifications.
Total Float: Time an activity can be delayed without delaying the relevant project or milestone completion under the model.
Total Float Calculation Type: Setting determining whether total float is derived from finish float, start float or the smaller of the two.
Total Float Value Method: Delay identification based on comparing total float values between programme updates rather than tracing driving logic.
Tower Crane: Fixed or climbing crane serving a building footprint, whose erection, climbs and dismantle are frequent programme constraints.
TQ: Technical Query [generic] | Technical Query/Queries [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
TRA: Time Risk Allowance [generic] | Task Risk Assessment. [generic]
Traceability: Ability to trace material, work or a record back to its source and supporting documentation.
Track Alignment: Horizontal and vertical geometry of the track, defined by radii, gradients, transitions and cant.
Track Slab: Concrete or structural base supporting rails in slab-track construction.
Traction Power: Electrical power system supplying vehicles for propulsion.
Traction Power Substation: Facility converting distribution network supply to the voltage and form required by the traction system.
Trade Contractor: Specialist contractor engaged directly by the client under a management arrangement.
Trade Stacking: Concentration of multiple trades in the same area at the same time, reducing productivity.
Traffic Management: Planning and control of vehicle, pedestrian, and work-zone movements during construction.
Traffic Management Plan: Plan for maintaining traffic movement and safety during works in or adjacent to the highway.
Train Detection: System establishing the presence of a vehicle on a section of track, such as track circuits or axle counters.
Training: Instruction of the operator's staff in the operation and maintenance of installed systems.
Trakhees: Regulatory arm of Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation, licensing and approving development in certain Dubai jurisdictions. [UAE]
Tram-Train: Vehicle capable of operating on both street tramway and main line railway infrastructure.
Tramco: Tram vehicle supply and maintenance contract for the Edinburgh Tram Project.
Tramstop: Passenger boarding point on a tramway, generally with low platform and shelter rather than full station facilities.
Tramway: Rail system operating wholly or partly on street, sharing space with other traffic.
Transformer: Device changing voltage between distribution and utilisation levels.
Transmittal: Formal record of documents or data issued from one party to another.
Transom: Horizontal framing member in a facade system.
Trenchless: Techniques installing pipes and ducts without continuous open excavation.
Trend: Emerging potential change or forecast movement tracked before formal approval.
Trend Register: Log of potential changes and emerging cost or schedule effects pending disposition.
Trial Erection: Assembly in the fabrication works to verify fit before delivery to site.
Trial Hole: Targeted excavation used to verify the position, depth, type, or condition of underground services or ground.
Trial Operations: Controlled pre-opening operation used to demonstrate integrated readiness, procedures, and performance.
Trial Pit: Shallow excavation to expose and log near-surface ground conditions and obstructions.
Trial Running: Extended running of vehicles to timetable without passengers to demonstrate reliability before entry into service.
Triangulation: Comparison of multiple independent evidence streams to test an inferred path, event, or date.
Tribunal: Arbitrator or panel of arbitrators appointed to determine a dispute.
Trigger Level: Predefined monitoring threshold at which specified actions must be taken.
True Concurrent Delay: An employer-risk and contractor-risk delay whose critical effects occur at the same time and each effectively delays completion.
True Value Adjudication: Adjudication determining the correct valuation of work, following or resisting a smash and grab decision.
TS ETFR: Transport Scotland Edinburgh Tram Fortnightly Report
TSC: NEC4 TSC [NEC] | Tram Sub Committee [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
TTRO: Temporary Traffic Regulation Order. [UK infrastructure] | Temporary Traffic Regulation Order. See Traffic Regulation Order [Edinburgh Tram Inquiry]
Tunnel Boring Machine: Machine excavating a tunnel at full face while erecting or supporting the lining behind it.
Turnaround: Planned shutdown of an operating facility for inspection, maintenance and modification.
Turnout: Assembly of switches and crossings permitting a vehicle to move from one track to another.
Two-Stage Tender: Procurement approach appointing a contractor on outline terms, with the price fixed after design development.
U-Value: Measure of thermal transmittance through a building element.
UAE Civil Code: Federal Law No. 5 of 1985 concerning Civil Transactions, the principal source of contract and construction law in onshore UAE. [UAE]
UDFTYPE: P6 XER table containing user-defined-field definitions.
UDFVALUE: P6 XER table containing user-defined-field values.
Ultrasonic Testing: Non-destructive method detecting internal flaws using high-frequency sound.
Unabsorbed Overhead: Head office overhead that could not be recovered because turnover was reduced or delayed.
UNCITRAL: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law; source of widely used arbitration rules and model law.
Undefined Provisional Sum: Provisional sum for work insufficiently described, entitling the contractor to time and preliminaries consequences when instructed.
Underpinning: Strengthening or deepening of an existing foundation to carry additional load or permit adjacent excavation.
Undistributed Budget: Budget for authorised work not yet allocated to control accounts.
Unexplained Interruption: Gap in the execution of an activity with no identified driving cause in the available programme record. [toolkit]
Unforeseeable Physical Conditions: Natural or man-made conditions encountered on site that an experienced contractor could not reasonably have foreseen at tender. [FIDIC]
Unimpacted Programme: Reference programme before the modeled event is applied.
Unitised Facade: Curtain wall delivered as factory-assembled units installed directly onto the frame.
Units Percent Complete: Progress measure based on actual and remaining labour or non-labour units.
Unjust Enrichment: Doctrine permitting recovery where one party has been enriched at another's expense without legal justification.
Unsupported Claim: Assertion in a generated output that cannot be traced to a cited source.
Update Selection: Documented choice of the programme update representing the contemporaneous state for a period or event.
Update Window: Analysis window bounded by two consecutive contemporaneous programme updates.
Updated Programme: Accepted or reference programme statused with actual progress and revised forecast information.
UPS System: Uninterruptible power supply maintaining supply during transfer or outage.
Utilities Diversion: Relocation, protection, abandonment, or modification of existing utility services to enable the works.
Utility Conflict: Clash between proposed works and an existing or planned utility asset.
Utility Connection: Physical and contractual connection to a network operator's infrastructure.
Utility Survey: Investigation to establish the position and nature of buried services, by desktop study, geophysics and trial excavation.
VAC: Variance at Completion [generic] | Variance at Completion; difference between BAC and EAC. [generic]
Value Engineering: Structured review seeking required function at improved whole-life value without unacceptable loss of performance.
Value Stream Mapping: Analysis of the steps in a process to identify and remove non-value-adding activity.
Van Oord v Allseas: Van Oord UK Ltd v Allseas UK Ltd [2015] EWHC 3074 (TCC); judicial criticism of unsubstantiated claims and expert reliance on unverified assertions. [Case law]
Vapour Control Layer: Membrane limiting moisture migration through a construction build-up.
Variance: Quantified difference between baseline, forecast, actual, or target values.
Variance Analysis Report: Periodic explanation of cost and schedule variances, their causes, impact and corrective actions.
Variance at Completion: Difference between Budget at Completion and Estimate at Completion.
Variation: Contractual change to the scope, quantity, quality, sequence, method, or conditions of the works.
Variation Account: Running record of instructed changes, their valuation and their status.
Variation Order: Formal instruction or agreement varying the contractual works.
Variation Register: Log of potential and instructed variations, valuation, time effect, and status.
VAV: Variable Air Volume; ventilation control varying supply volume to meet zone demand.
Vector Database: Database optimized to store and search vector embeddings.
Vendor Data: Supplier-issued drawings, calculations and manuals required for design coordination and handover.
Verification and Validation: Confirmation that a system was built correctly and that it meets the operational need.
Vesting Certificate: Document transferring ownership of materials to the employer before delivery to site.
Vibration Monitoring: Measurement of ground-borne vibration against limits protecting adjacent structures and occupants.
Vibro Compaction: Densification of granular soils using a depth vibrator, with or without stone backfill.
Visual Management: Use of visual displays at the workplace to make status, targets and problems immediately apparent.
Visual Mock-Up: Sample assembly built to confirm appearance and workmanship before production.
Volume Loss: Ground volume lost during tunnelling, expressed as a proportion of the excavated volume and used to predict settlement.
Volumetric Modular: Three-dimensional units manufactured off site and assembled to form a building.
Voluntary Acceleration: Acceleration chosen by the contractor without a contractual instruction or established employer liability.
Wage Protection System: UAE electronic salary transfer system, compliance with which is a condition of labour and permit renewals. [UAE]
Wait-and-See Approach: Deferring delay assessment until effects are fully known, contrary to contemporaneous management where the contract permits earlier assessment.
Waiver: Intentional relinquishment of a known right, assessed under the applicable law.
Walter Lilly: Walter Lilly & Co Ltd v Mackay [2012] EWHC 1773 (TCC); English authority on concurrency, global claims and the importance of records. [Case law]
Warranty: Contractual assurance regarding performance, quality, or correction of defects for a stated period.
Waste: Any activity consuming resources without adding value, including waiting, rework, transport and overproduction.
Watching Brief: Archaeological or environmental monitoring of excavation works under a planning or consent condition.
Water Balancing: Regulation of flow rates through a system to achieve design volumes at each terminal.
Water Ingress: Unintended entry of water into a building, a common source of defect and delay disputes.
Water Table: Level below which the ground is saturated.
Water Treatment Works: Facility treating raw water to potable standard.
Waterproofing: Measures preventing water ingress into a structure.
Wayleave: Agreement granting rights to install, access, inspect, or maintain apparatus on land.
WBS Summary Activity: P6 activity summarizing dates of activities within a WBS branch.
Weather Record: Dated record of weather conditions relevant to work progress or safety.
Weather Standby: Idle time and cost where work cannot proceed because of weather.
Weather Window: Forecast period of conditions permitting a weather-sensitive operation, a central concept in marine and lifting programmes.
Webhook: HTTP callback sent automatically when a defined event occurs.
Weekly Progress Report: Weekly summary of progress, planned work, constraints, resources, events, and actions.
Weighted Progress: Progress calculated by applying agreed weights to quantities, activities, or milestones.
Weld Procedure Specification: Approved document defining the parameters for making a qualified weld.
Welded Connection: Joint made by fusion, requiring qualified procedures, welders and inspection.
Welfare Facilities: Statutory provision of sanitary, washing, rest and changing facilities for the workforce.
WELL: Certification scheme addressing building features affecting occupant health and wellbeing.
Wellpoint: Closely spaced shallow dewatering points connected to a suction header.
Wet Riser: Permanently charged firefighting main within a building.
What-If Analysis: Scenario calculation testing how specified changes to logic, duration, constraints, or resources affect forecast dates.
Wheel Wash: Facility cleaning vehicle wheels before leaving site to prevent highway contamination.
Whole Life Carbon: Combined embodied and operational emissions across an asset's life.
Window: Discrete period of the project selected for separate delay analysis, usually bounded by programme updates or key events.
Window Boundary: Start or end date defining an analysis window, typically a data date, milestone or significant event.
Windows Analysis: Period-by-period analysis of changing critical or driving paths, progress, and delay events.
Without Prejudice: Label and legal principle potentially protecting genuine settlement communications from use as admissions.
Witness Point: Point at which a nominated party may attend, but which does not prevent progress if they do not.
Witness Statement: Signed written evidence of a witness's factual account.
Witness Testing: Testing observed and signed off by the client, consultant or authority.
Work Authorization Document: Document formally releasing scope, budget and schedule to a control account manager.
Work Breakdown Structure: Hierarchical decomposition of project scope into manageable deliverables and work packages.
Work Front: Physical area made available for a crew to work in, the practical unit of progress on site.
Work Front Availability: Extent to which areas are released free of preceding trades, obstructions and defects.
Work Package: Lowest WBS component for which cost and duration can be estimated and managed.
Work Sampling: Observational technique recording the proportion of time crews spend on direct work, support work and delay.
Workface Planning: Detailed planning that makes installation work ready with labour, materials, information, access, and tools.
Working Hours Restriction: Consent condition limiting the times at which construction activity may take place.
Working Programme: Programme used by the site team to direct work, which may differ from the contractual programme.
Works Information: NEC3 defined term describing the works to be provided and constraints on how they are provided. [NEC]
Workweek: Recurring pattern of working and non-working hours in a calendar.
XER: Primavera P6 proprietary text exchange format containing project, activity, logic, calendar, resource, code, and related tables.
XER Parser: Software component that reads Primavera XER tables and converts them into typed programme data.
Z Clause: Additional condition of contract drafted by the client and appended to the NEC standard terms. [NEC]
Zero Data Retention: Arrangement under which submitted content is not stored by the provider after processing.
Zero Float: Condition in which an activity has no calculated total float to the relevant completion point.
Zero Float Constraint: Constraint forcing an activity's total float to zero and thereby placing it on the critical path artificially.
